Then the Lord will give wonders in heaven and on earth: in heaven, because the sun was turned into darkness and the moon into blood; on earth, because the earth trembled with so violent and unusual a motion that the tombs were opened and the rocks split. And as to his saying blood and vapors, or vapor of smoke, that blood is the one of which we read in the psalms: That your foot may be dipped in blood. And in Isaiah: How red are your garments. And the blood which, when the Savior's side was pierced, the Roman soldier shed mixed with water. And the fire of the Holy Spirit, which came down from heaven, as we read in the Acts of the Apostles: There appeared to them divided tongues as of fire, and it sat upon each of them, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit; and they began to speak in various tongues, as the Holy Spirit gave them to speak. This is the fire which the Lord came to send upon the earth, and which, before he suffered, he longed to burn in his disciples. Fire is of a double nature: it has light for believers, it has darkness and punishments for unbelievers, who are called vapors of smoke. This smoke is most bitter, which blinded the eyes of the Jews, of which we read in Proverbs: As smoke is harmful to the eyes, and an unripe grape to the teeth, so is iniquity to those who use it. Of this smoke Isaiah too speaks in the great vision in which the blindness of the Jews was foretold: And the lintel was moved, and the house was filled with smoke. Whence there follows afterwards: Go, and say to this people: Hearing you shall hear, and shall not understand, and seeing you shall look, and shall not see; for the heart of this people has been made gross, and with their ears they have heard heavily. The sun too was turned into darkness, when it did not dare to look upon its Lord hanging, and the moon into blood; which either we should believe happened according to the history and was passed over in silence by the evangelists, for not all the things that Jesus did are reported as written; which if they were written one by one, I think that not even the world itself could contain the books that would have to be written; or certainly, as the sun was turned into darkness, not that it was itself changed into darkness, but that it brought darkness upon the world, so also the moon was not turned into blood, but condemned the Jews, covered with the horror of blasphemies and of denial against Christ, by the eternal blood of their own testimony, as they said: His blood be upon us, and upon our children.
Commentary on Joel

He describes all these things as to come before the great and dreadful day of the Lord comes. But the great and dreadful day of the Lord is to be believed to be either that of the resurrection, or certainly, many ages later, the day of judgment, which is truly great and dreadful. But since there follows: And it shall be, everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord shall be saved, and the apostle Paul refers this to the time of the Lord's passion, it is rather to be understood of the day of the resurrection. For he says, writing to the Romans: There is no distinction of Jew and Greek. For the same one is Lord of all: rich toward all who call upon him. For everyone, whoever calls upon the name of the Lord, shall be saved. How then shall they call upon him in whom they have not believed? Or how shall they believe him whom they have not heard? And how shall they hear without a preacher? And how shall they preach unless they are sent. And as to his saying: Everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord shall be saved, let us believe that it is no light thing; for although the same Apostle writes: No one says Lord Jesus except in the Holy Spirit; yet this very saying is to be weighed not by speech but by the affection of the heart. For everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord shall be saved. Hence Paul and Sosthenes also write to the Church of God which is at Corinth: To those sanctified in Christ Jesus, called saints, with all who call upon the name of the Lord Jesus Christ; according to what we read in the psalms: Moses and Aaron among his priests, and Samuel among those who call upon his name. They called upon the Lord, and he heard them; in the pillar of cloud he spoke to them. If, therefore, it is written of the believing Corinthians, and of Moses and Aaron and Samuel, that they called upon the name of the Lord, let us believe that this grace belongs not to beginners, but to the perfect.

For in mount Zion and in Jerusalem there shall be salvation, as the Lord has said; and in the remnant whom the Lord shall call. LXX: For in mount Zion and in Jerusalem there shall be he who has been saved? As the Lord has said, and announcing those whom the Lord called. In the place where we have put salvation, or the one saved, and in the Hebrew is written phaleta, Symmachus translated, he who has fled. And again, where we said, in the remnant, and the LXX translated, announcing, in the Hebrew is read saridim, which the Jews think is the name of a place. After, therefore, the great and dreadful day of the Lord came, and whoever after the Lord's resurrection called upon his name was made safe, everyone who was on mount Zion and in Jerusalem was saved; for out of Zion went forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem, of which it is written: It cannot be that a prophet perish outside Jerusalem. The beginning, then, of those who were saved was in Zion and Jerusalem, in the watchtower and in the vision of peace, and in those who were the remnant, whom the Lord called. By the remnant we ought to understand those of the people of the Jews who believed, of whom Isaiah speaks: Unless the Lord of Sabaoth had left us seed, we would have become like Sodom, and we would have been like Gomorrah. These, the remnant, the Lord called, or he evangelized those whom he called: for so the LXX translated.

When the holy apostle wished to show that the prophets had foretold the coming of those times when it should come to pass that all nations would believe in God, he cited the testimony that reads, "And it shall come to pass that everyone who calls on the name of the Lord shall be saved." For the name of God who has made heaven and earth used to be invoked among the Israelites only. The rest of the nations used to call upon deaf and dumb idols and were not heard by them; or they invoked demons and were heard to their own harm. "But when the fullness of time had come," then was fulfilled what had been foretold. "And it shall come to pass, that everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord shall be saved." Hence the Jews—even those of them who believed in Christ—begrudged the gospel of the Gentiles and maintained that the gospel of Christ ought not to be preached to the uncircumcised.

For behold, in those days and at that time, when I shall turn back the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem, I will gather all the nations, and I will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat, and I will plead with them there over my people and my inheritance Israel, whom they have scattered among the nations; and they have divided my land, and over my people they have cast the lot; and they have put a boy in a brothel, and sold a girl for wine, that they might drink. LXX: For behold, I, in those days and at that time, when I shall turn back the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem, will gather all the nations, and I will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat, and I will plead with them there for my people and my inheritance Israel, who have been scattered among the Gentiles; and they have divided my land, and over my people they have cast lots; and they have put a boy in a brothel, and they were selling girls for wine, and they were drinking. Let us speak as we promised: first, according to anagogy, joining what comes after to what went before; then, if we can, we shall try to refer the same things to the day of judgment. When the believers have been saved on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, and the remnant of the people of the Jews, who believed with the apostles and through the apostles, has been called, at that time, after the Lord, who had come to preach sight to the blind and release to the captives, has turned back the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem, and has set free those who confess the Lord and who dwell in the Church, in which is the vision of peace, he will gather all the nations that refused to believe, and will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat; which, according to the Hebrew truth, is said more expressively in Greek κατάξω, that is, I will lead downward, and draw down from the heights to lower places. And consider at the same time that when the Lord summons all unbelievers, or the adverse powers, to judgment, and pleads with them for his people: I will bring them down, he says, into the valley of Jehoshaphat. But when he exhorts believers to battle, he says: Rouse the strong; let them approach, let all the men of war go up; let the nations arise and go up into the valley of Jehoshaphat: they are urged not to go down, but to go up. For everyone who is judged on account of his sins is placed in the valley which is called Jehoshaphat, that is, the judgment of the Lord. For he who believes in the Lord shall not be judged. And there he will dispute with them, convincing them not by the power of his majesty but by the truth of reason: those who have parted the people of God among themselves and have scattered his inheritance among the nations, so as to compel the servants of God to serve them; and who have divided his land, separating it among themselves by many errors, so that some worshiped Jupiter, others Juno, and Minerva, and Fever, and Blight, and Anubis, and the crocodile, and the ibis, owls, hawks and storks.

They also want those to be understood as men who, putting away the beginnings of little children, have come to the strength of mature age, and have turned all the zeal with which they formerly worked the fields of their souls to the need of battle. But to us, following the opinion of the Hebrews, it seems to be the opposite. For the nations hostile to Israel are made ready for battle, and change their ploughshares and mattocks, or sickles, into swords and spears, and the weak says he is strong, and they burst out and come from round about, and gather together against the army of the Lord, for this purpose: that the Lord may cause their strong ones to fall, and that they may understand that they have been overcome because God opposed them. These things wretched Israel promises itself according to the letter. We, following the tropology we have begun, can take them both of the nations of demons, and of those who daily fight against the Church, and in the end of those who under the Antichrist are going to fight against the saints of the Lord, who are gathered together for this purpose, that they may perish.
Commentary on Joel

Let them arise and go up into the valley of Jehoshaphat, for there I will sit to judge all the nations round about; put in the sickles, for the harvest is ripe. Come and go down, for the winepress is full; the vats overflow, for their wickedness is multiplied. LXX: Let all the nations arise and go up into the valley of Jehoshaphat, for there I will sit to judge all the nations round about; send forth the sickles, for the vintage is at hand. Come in and tread, for the winepress is full and the vats overflow, for their evils are filled up. These things too they interpret in two ways, following the sense given above. For some understand in a good sense that the nations go up into the valley of Jehoshaphat, which is interpreted the judgment of the Lord, and that God sits there to judge all the nations that come from round about: namely, that the saints too are gathered there against the adversaries of God, and put in their sickles to reap the ripe harvest of the enemy, and come and go down, and tread the winepresses, because the vintage is at hand, and the new wine overflows to such a degree that the vats cannot hold it. And so that we might know what the vintage and the full winepress are, he added: Their wickedness is multiplied, without doubt meaning those who have gathered together against the Lord. Others, however, assert that the nations arise and come together into the valley of Jehoshaphat, and that the Lord sits to judge all the nations, for this reason: that they may prepare themselves and take up all the arms of fighting men, and be mown down by the sickles of the Lord in the valley of Jehoshaphat. For the time of judgment, they say, has come against them, and their evils have grown so far as to overcome the patience of God. For the Amorites too were driven out at the time when their sins were fulfilled. The Jews refer this passage to Gog and Magog, most savage nations, of whom we spoke above, thinking that in the last time, when Jerusalem has been restored, they will come against the people of God under the thousand-year rule, and will fall in the valley of Jehoshaphat, which lies on the eastern side of the temple; for the time of their slaughter will have come, and the vintage of the shedding of blood be at hand.
Commentary on Joel

Peoples, peoples in the valley of cutting down, for the day of the Lord is near in the valley of cutting down. The sun and the moon have been darkened, and the stars have withdrawn their brightness. LXX: Sounds have been heard in the valley of judgment, for the day of the Lord is near in the valley of judgment. The sun and the moon will be darkened, and the stars will make their brightness set. In the place where we have put peoples, peoples, and the Seventy translated sounds have been heard, in the Hebrew is written amonim, amonim, which certainly signifies the multitude and the crowds of those who are to be judged, not noise and sound. Again, where we said in the valley of cutting down, following the translation of Aquila and Symmachus and the Fifth edition, the Seventy and Theodotion translated τῆς δίκης καί τῆς κρίσεως, that is, of the case and of judgment; in place of which in the Hebrew is written harus, which the Hebrews think means not only cutting down but also gold: namely, that in the valley of judgment, which they suppose to be Gehenna, when the dross of sins has been burned out, pure gold may remain. And the peoples of the nations of which we spoke above are gathered in the valley of judgment, or of cutting down, for this reason: that they may be slain and fall, and be judged by the Lord.
Commentary on Joel

The grief of that day and the torments of those who perish not even the sun and moon and the other stars will be able to look upon, but they will withdraw their brightness, and will not dare to behold the severity of him who judges and renders each one's work upon his own head. Not that they are more merciful than the judgments of God, but that every creature, at the torments of others, trembles for its own judgment.
Commentary on Joel

And the Lord will roar from Zion, and from Jerusalem he will utter his voice, and the heavens and the earth will be moved; and the Lord is the hope of his people and the strength of the sons of Israel; and you will know that I am the Lord your God, dwelling in Zion, my holy mountain; and Jerusalem will be holy, and strangers will not pass through her any more. LXX: But the Lord will cry out from Zion, and from Jerusalem he will utter his voice, and heaven and earth will be moved; and the Lord will spare his people, and will strengthen the sons of Israel; and you will know that I am the Lord your God, dwelling in Zion, my holy mountain; and Jerusalem will be holy, and the foreigner will not pass through her any more. When the brightness of the sun and moon and all the stars has been changed into darkness, the Lord will roar from Zion like a lion, or cry out; and his voice will be so loud and terrible that the hinges of the heavens and the foundations of the earth will be shaken. And though he will be so severe toward those who are to be punished, he will be merciful toward his people, and will give strength to those who are called the sons of Israel, that is, a mind seeing God; or εὐθύτατος Θεοῦ, which we can call the most upright of God; those who have not walked in crooked paths, but, going in the way of Christ, have done all things rightly.
Commentary on Joel

Then both those who will be punished and those who will be taken up into glory will know that the Lord dwells in his watchtower Zion, and in Christ, his holy mountain, or in him who has prepared himself as a worthy dwelling place of God. Then Jerusalem, the vision of peace, will be holy, from which Solomon too received his name, and strangers will not pass through her any more. Understand by strangers either the demons, who are alien to God, or all the worst thoughts and sins, of which the prophet speaks: From strangers spare your servant; which would by no means find a way into us any more, if we have the peace of God and our heart has not lain open to the adversaries. These things the Jews and, as we have said, our Judaizers refer to the fable of the thousand years, when they think that Christ will dwell in Zion, and that the peoples of the saints will be gathered into a Jerusalem of gold and gems, so that those who in this age have been oppressed by all the nations may in this same age rule over all the nations.
LETTERS 48:21

Christ himself is a virgin, and his mother is also a virgin; yes, though she is his mother, she is a virgin still. For Jesus has entered in through the closed doors, and in his sepulcher—a new one hewn out of the hardest rock—no man is laid either before him or after him. Mary is "a garden enclosed … a fountain sealed," and from that fountain flows, according to Joel, the river that waters the torrent bed either of cords or of thorns. The cords [are] those of the sins by which we were beforetime bound, the thorns those which choked the seed the good man of the house had sown.
Commentary on Joel

And it will be in that day: the mountains will drip sweetness, and the hills will flow with milk, and through all the streams of Judah waters will go. LXX: And it will be in that day: the mountains will drip sweetness, and the hills will flow with milk, and all the outlets of Judah will flow with waters. When the Lord dwells in Zion and on his holy mountain, when no one will attempt to pass through holy Jerusalem, whoever in her is a mountain, and has reached the heights of the virtues, will sweat sweetness and honey; and from him will drip spiritual graces, of which the prophet speaks: How sweet are your words to my throat, above honey to my mouth. But he who is lower than the mountains, and has not yet climbed to the summit of perfection, will be called a hill, and from him will flow streams of milk, by which the untaught infancy in Christ is nourished, and the rivers of water which the Lord testified would flow from his belly. For all the streams, or outlets, of Judah will be filled with waters, and nothing in them will be dry, since all things overflow with spiritual grace.

And a fountain will go forth from the house of the Lord and will water the torrent of thorns. For the torrent of thorns the Seventy translated the torrent of cords, that is, σχοίνων, which means either cords or, among the Egyptians, the measure of a fixed stretch of road, as the psalmist says: My path and my cord you have searched out. For on the river Nile, or in its channels, they are accustomed to haul ships with ropes, having fixed stretches, which they call cords, so that fresh necks of haulers may take over the labor of the exhausted. Nor is it any wonder if each nation calls the fixed stretches of roads by its own names, since the Latins speak of a thousand paces, the Gauls of leagues, the Persians of parasangs, and all Germany of rastae, and with each of these names the measure is different. I say this because the Seventy translated the Hebrew word settim as cords. Moreover, no one doubts that everything we read of in the tabernacle of God was made of settim wood, which the LXX rendered incorruptible wood. Now it is a kind of tree in the desert, like the white thorn in color and leaves, not in size. For otherwise the trees are so large that very broad planks are cut from them, and the wood is very strong, and of incredible lightness and beauty, so that all the wealthiest and most painstaking even make from it the vessels of the winepresses, which they call ἄρσενας (males) and θηλύας (females); and this wood is not found in cultivated places and on Roman soil, apart from the desert of Arabia. For the torrent of cords, or of thorns, Symmachus rendered the valley of thorns. Now there is a place near Livias, beyond the Dead Sea, six miles distant from Livias, where Israel once committed fornication with the Midianites. This place the prophet Micah mentions in the person of God, saying: My people, remember, I pray, what Balak king of Moab devised, and what Balaam son of Beor answered, from Settim to Gilgal. For which there too the Seventy translated ἀπὸ τῶν σχοίνων, that is, from the cords to Gilgal. Therefore a fountain will go forth from the house of the Lord, which is interpreted as the Church. Of this Ezekiel and Zechariah also write at the end of their books: that they may change our thorns, and vices and sins, which have borne no fruit of righteousness, into the Lord's new-broken fields, and water our dryness with most abundant waters, and that instead of thorns and briars we may bring forth manifold flowers of the virtues. And in that place where Israel once committed fornication and was initiated into Baal-peor, may lilies of chastity and roses of modesty and virginity abound.
Commentary on Joel

Egypt will be a desolation, and Idumea a desert of perdition, because they have acted wickedly against the sons of Judah, and have shed innocent blood in their land. LXX: Egypt will be in perdition, and Idumea a plain of desolation, because of the iniquities of the sons of Judah, because they have shed righteous blood in their land. In this place too the Jews sleep a very heavy sleep, imagining with a most vain hope that in the last time, when they are to receive not Christ but the Antichrist, there will be vengeance for them upon the Egyptians, who are their neighbors, and upon the Romans, whom they interpret as the Idumeans: namely, that just as Pharaoh and all his army, who held the people of God captive for four hundred and thirty years, were drowned in the Red Sea, so also the Romans, who are to possess the Jews for the same span of years, may be destroyed by the vengeance of the Lord. Let them promise themselves this with an empty hope. For they cannot explain why, when there are so many nations in the world, two nations alone, the Egyptians and the Idumeans, are singled out for punishment; or why the Romans should be understood by the Idumeans, when with the same license of lying we could on the contrary assert that under the name of the Idumeans either the Persians, or the Elamites, or the Franks, the Alamanni, and other nations are signified. But let us say that at the time of the Lord's resurrection, or on the day of judgment — for we accept both —, both Egypt and Idumea are to be destroyed, insofar as they are Egypt and Idumea. Egypt is called mesraim, which is interpreted ἐκθλίβουσα, that is, persecuting and afflicting the saints of God; Idumea, earthly, or bloody. Whoever, therefore, has persecuted the people of God, and has given himself to earthly works, and by a multitude of offenses has daily shed innocent blood, the blood, namely, of those whom he deceives, will be brought to perdition, just as we know that the souls of the martyrs too cry out under the altar: How long, O Lord, holy and true, do you not judge and avenge our blood on those who dwell on the earth?
Commentary on Joel

And Judea will be inhabited for ever, and Jerusalem to generation and generation; and I will cleanse their blood, which I had not cleansed; and the Lord will abide in Zion. LXX: But Judea will be inhabited for ever, and Jerusalem to generations of generations; and I will seek out their blood, and will not suffer it to be unavenged. And the Lord will dwell in Zion. Surely it is not this Judea that will be inhabited for ever, which we see to be deserted, nor this Jerusalem, whose ruins we behold, but that Judea whose daughters have exulted and rejoiced in all the judgments of the Lord, and of which we read at the end of the fiftieth (51st) psalm: Deal kindly, O Lord, in your good will with Zion, that the walls of Jerusalem may be built. In this province of confession and glory, and in this city in which the peace of the Lord is seen, there will be an eternal habitation, not for one, or for three or more generations, but to generation and generation, that is, in the two generations of those who have believed from the Jews and from the Gentiles.
Commentary on Joel

And the Lord will cleanse the blood of all sins, which he had not cleansed before, so as to cleanse in the Gospel those whom, sinning under the law, he had left unclean. For he has shut up all things under sin for this purpose, that he may have mercy on all; or he will avenge the blood of his servants, which they have shed in martyrdom for the confession of his name. And the Lord will abide in Zion, of which it is written: Its foundations are on the holy mountains; the Lord loves the gates of Zion above all the tents of Jacob.

intro: THE PROPHECY OF JOEL. INTRODUCTION. Joel, whose name, according to St. Jerome, signifies the Lord God, (or, as others say, the coming down of God) prophesied about the same time in the kingdom of Juda as Osee did in the kingdom of Israel. He foretells, under figures, the great evils that were coming upon the people for their sins; earnestly exhorts them to repentance, and comforts them with the promise of a teacher of justice, viz., Christ Jesus, our Lord, and of the coming down of his Holy Spirit (Challoner) upon the hundred and twenty faithful assembled in Sion. [Acts i. 15. and ii. 4.] He describes the land of the twelve tribes made desolate, and the people cast off. (St. Jerome ad Paulin.) --- Yet he speaks chiefly of the kingdom of Juda, and mentions the house of God, sacrifices, &c. (Worthington) --- St. Jerome infers from his being placed after Osee, without any fresh title, (Calmet) that he lived in that order of time. (Worthington) --- But this rule is not general, as Jonas lived before Amos; and [the] Septuagint observe not the same disposition of the prophets as we do. The exact time of the famine, when Joel prophesied, cannot be ascertained. It seems he addressed the people in autumn, when a second year's famine was apprehended. He paints every thing with great force and beauty of style. (Calmet)
